text:
jordan: Hey team, onboarding day 2. Got a refurbished MacBook Air (M2) from the kit, asset RWI-0821. During setup MDM enrollment started but then I got an error 'Enrollment blocked: device associated with another Apple ID'. FileVault prompt never showed. Anyone seen this?
it-support: Hi Jordan, welcome! Quick Q: did you sign in to iCloud with a personal Apple ID during setup? That can block DEP/Automated Enrollment. If you haven't completed setup, please reboot into Recovery and choose to continue the Setup Assistant without signing into iCloud. If you've already completed, we can try wiping it remotely.
jordan: I did sign in briefly to restore apps. Oops. Is a wipe required? I have some personal files but nothing major.
mac-admin: If the device is enrolled in Apple Business Manager to our org, personal Apple ID association can prevent MDM from taking ownership. We can clear the association if you factory-reset it and then skip iCloud sign-in. I can coordinate a remote erase via our MDM, but it only works if the device shows up as managed. What do you see in Settings > General > About > Enrollment?
jordan: Settings > About shows 'Not managed'. The serial is C02Y9ZZZZZ and asset tag RWI-0821.
it-support: Ok, two paths: a) If you're comfortable, we can walk you through a local wipe (Recovery -> Erase Mac and reinstall macOS) and re-run setup while skipping iCloud. b) If you prefer remote, we can attempt to add the device to ABM and reassign, but that may need shipping back to IT for Apple-side un-association. Which do you prefer?
jordan: I'll do the local wipe. Can you send a checklist? Don't want to brick it.
it-support: Steps: 1) Backup any local files to an external drive or iCloud Drive. 2) Reboot holding the power button to get to Recovery. 3) Use Disk Utility -> Erase Internal SSD (APFS) -> Quit Disk Utility. 4) Reinstall macOS from Recovery, follow Setup Assistant but DO NOT sign into iCloud or Apple ID. 5) Once at desktop, connect to wifi; you should get a "Corporate device enrollment requested" prompt from our MDM. Complete Okta SSO when prompted.
mac-admin: I'll also pre-allocate a zero-touch token for RWI-0821 so it should auto-enroll once you reach the Setup Assistant and connect to Wi-Fi.
jordan: Doing the erase now. Quick question: if FileVault doesn't prompt again, how do I enable it?
it-support: After enrollment completes, we'll push a FileVault enable profile which triggers the enable flow and escrow. If you don't see the modal within 10 minutes, run `sudo fdesetup status` and ping us.
jordan: Reinstalling now. Might be 15min.
(20 minutes later)
jordan: Back — completed reinstall, skipped Apple ID, got the MDM prompt, completed Okta SSO. `sudo profiles status -type enrollment` shows enrolled.
it-support: Nice. I'm pushing FileVault enable now. Expect a System Settings modal to enable and choose recovery escrow.
jordan: Prompt showed, I chose to escrow to KMS. `sudo fdesetup status` -> FileVault On. All good.
ops-oncall: Inventory note: serial C02Y9ZZZZZ -> RWI-0821, user jordan assigned, dev tools allowed.
mdm-bot: Notice: Enrollment completed and FileVault escrow confirmed for RWI-0821 at 2026-05-10T11:48:12Z.
jordan: Thanks everyone for the patient walkthrough 60a Closing thread.
